scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-05.statement: Monthly dispute ticket volume: 610 (2026-06), 590 (2026-07), 1180 (2026-08), 1260 (2026-09), roughly doubling from the Jun-Jul baseline and continuing to rise in September.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-GAP.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a ticket-handling capacity/speed problem (CS cannot answer disputes fast enough), so an auto-answering agent is the correct fix.

H-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August caused bills to be computed/accepted incorrectly (e.g., wrong read acceptance or estimate logic), driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-DATA-GAP.statement: AMI (MDMS) interval reads failed to deliver or were invalid starting around August, forcing estimate substitution and incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-READ-GAP.statement: Manual field meter reads became incomplete or delayed around August, forcing more estimate substitutions and wrong bills.

H-CROSS-SYSTEM-MAPPING.statement: Reads from AMI and/or field sources are being delivered but misinterpreted or mismatched by the billing import (a handoff/semantic defect) rather than a single-source outage, producing wrong bills.

H-HIGHCONSUMPTION-REJECT.statement: Billing import rejects accepted, on-time AMI reads under a 'high consumption' validation check (billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution despite valid read data and accounting for most ESTIMATED-read disputes.

interpretation_history.interpretation: CRM data shows median dispute-response time 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, i.e. CS is largely meeting its response SLA despite the ticket surge. This weighs against ticket-handling speed/capacity being the surge's primary driver and says nothing about why bills are wrong.

The billing-db tariff_change_log query returned zero records, meaning no tariff/pricing changes were logged in the queried period. This rules out a tariff rate change as a contributing cause of the wrong bills, but says nothing about AMI delivery, field reads, cross-system mapping, or import validation rules.

Of disputed bills, 1785 involve an ACTUAL read and 1240 involve an ESTIMATED read, so a majority (59%) of disputes come from bills built on actual meter reads, not estimate substitution. This means the wrong-bill problem is not confined to cases where no read was accepted; something is also producing bad bills when a real read exists.

E-04.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL's statement that there has been no tariff change this year is a non-authoritative stakeholder claim that corroborates the already-recorded authoritative finding (E-02) that the tariff_change_log has zero changes; it adds no new weight to any current hypothesis since none of them attribute the wrong-bill cause to tariff/pricing changes.

Field manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts, i.e. there is a measurable shortfall in field read-route completion during the dispute-surge window. This says nothing about AMI delivery, cross-system mapping, or import rule changes, and it does not by itself establish what share of disputes the shortfall explains.

crm-tickets.dispute_volume_monthly shows disputes at 610 (Jun) and 590 (Jul) rising to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) — roughly double the Jun-Jul baseline and still climbing in September. This confirms the magnitude and timing of the surge referenced in the initial request but says nothing about its cause.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (non-authoritative) claims field reading has been short three readers since July, causing routes to run late and the affected customers' bills to be built on estimated reads instead of actual ones. This offers a candidate causal mechanism for the route-completion shortfall already observed in E-05, but it is an interested party's self-report (SH-FIELD has an incentive to attribute problems to staffing in order to grow headcount) and is not corroborated by any read-type or route data showing the shortfall is driven specifically by the July staffing drop.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract clause (E-08) establishes that the utility can request field route priority changes but execution requires Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) confirmation, reaffirming the authorization structure already encoded as K-DISPATCH; it says nothing about the cause of the billing dispute surge.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes (E-09) returned 14 route-level records with distinct completion values (sample: route R-00 at 0.7 completion), giving per-route granularity beneath the aggregate 0.88 completion already seen in E-05. This is only the field-side half of the planned cross-reference (W-WI-HANDOFFVERIFYCOMPARE); it does not yet show which disputed or estimated-bill accounts map to these 14 lagging routes.

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle (E-10) shows 320 accounts billed on an estimated read last cycle, spanning 40 distinct routes (sample AC-20000 on R-00); this is the billing-side half of the planned W-WI-HANDOFFVERIFYCOMPARE cross-reference against the 14 lagging routes already seen in E-09. The counts and the single sample alone do not show which of the 40 routes overlap with the 14 lagging routes, so no correlation conclusion can be drawn yet.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (non-authoritative) claims MDMS export access for Lakeside is now provisioned per vendor ticket TX-4471. If true this would unblock the previously ACCESS_PENDING mdms-export query, but the observation itself contains no AMI read-event data and does not confirm or refute any causal hypothesis.

Of the 1240 disputed bills with an ESTIMATED read (E-03), direct AMI read-event data (E-12) shows 1184 (95.5%) actually had an on-time AMI read that was then rejected by billing import with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, and only 56 (4.5%) truly had no AMI read received. This means the ESTIMATED-read dispute subset is overwhelmingly caused by billing import rejecting valid, on-time AMI reads under a high-consumption check, not by AMI delivery failure or (mainly) field read gaps.

U-RULECHANGECONFIRMED.question: Did the billing import validation rule change log (DA-RULES / billing-config) actually record a change around August, and does it correlate with the disputed ACTUAL-read bills?
U-RULECHANGECONFIRMED.decision_impact: Determines whether H-RULE-CHANGE or H-CROSS-SYSTEM-MAPPING is the confirmed mechanism, which gates any future manual bill correction.
U-RULECHANGECONFIRMED.resolution_path: Run query_billing_rule_change_log against DA-RULES (billing-config) and compare any change dates to the start of the August dispute surge.
U-RULECHANGECONFIRMED.safe_placeholder: Treat H-RULE-CHANGE and H-CROSS-SYSTEM-MAPPING as co-equal candidate mechanisms and run only diagnostic/read-only verification steps until one is confirmed.

U-AMIDELIVERYUNRESOLVED.question: Is AMI/MDMS read delivery actually healthy during the surge, given that mdms-export is DEGRADED and vendor export access is ACCESS_PENDING, so no direct AMI read-event data has been examined?
U-AMIDELIVERYUNRESOLVED.decision_impact: Affects whether the cross-system-mapping hypothesis traces to an AMI-side delivery problem versus a pure billing-import mapping defect, and whether mdms-export's degraded state masks a contributing cause.
U-AMIDELIVERYUNRESOLVED.resolution_path: Escalate to ORG-AMI vendor to provision mdms-export access, then run query_mdms_read_events and verify_handoff_semantic_validity on H-MDMS-BILL once restored.
U-AMIDELIVERYUNRESOLVED.safe_placeholder: Proceed with cross-system mapping analysis using only billing-db read_type data, and flag any mechanism conclusion that depends on direct AMI read-event data as provisional until mdms-export is restored.
U-AMIDELIVERYUNRESOLVED.resolution: Direct AMI read-event data (E-12) for the disputed-ESTIMATED cohort shows 1184/1240 (95.5%) had an AMI read received before cutoff, so AMI/MDMS delivery was largely healthy during the surge; the estimate substitutions are mostly explained by billing import rejecting those valid reads (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), not by AMI delivery failure.

U-FIELDSTAFFINGATTRIBUTION.question: Does the field route completion shortfall (E-05) actually correlate with the July staffing shortage SH-FIELD self-reports (E-07, non-authoritative, incentive to grow headcount), and does it explain the 41% ESTIMATED-read dispute subset?
U-FIELDSTAFFINGATTRIBUTION.decision_impact: Determines whether any route-priority change via push_route_update would meaningfully reduce ESTIMATED-read disputes or is addressing an unrelated/overstated factor.
U-FIELDSTAFFINGATTRIBUTION.resolution_path: Cross-check route-log completion shortfall timing/accounts against field staffing records (if obtainable) rather than relying solely on SH-FIELD's self-report (E-07).
U-FIELDSTAFFINGATTRIBUTION.safe_placeholder: Treat the field-route shortfall as a secondary factor limited to part of the ESTIMATED-read subset; do not attribute causal weight to the staffing claim (E-07) without corroboration.

U-BASELINETRENDVALIDITY.question: Does the continuing rise in disputes from Aug (1180) to Sep (1260) mean the defect is still active/worsening, so a single-month snapshot is not a valid success measurement?
U-BASELINETRENDVALIDITY.decision_impact: Affects whether SC-DISPUTEBASELINE's threshold can be evaluated on one month of data or must wait for the trend to stabilize after a fix is deployed.
U-BASELINETRENDVALIDITY.resolution_path: Continue track_dispute_volume_trend monthly and re-evaluate against baseline once at least two consecutive months show a stable trend post-fix.
U-BASELINETRENDVALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Treat the dispute-baseline threshold as provisional pending at least two consecutive months of trend data; do not declare success on a single-month snapshot.

A-READTYPESPLITREPRESENTATIVE.statement: The ACTUAL/ESTIMATED read-type split observed among disputed bills (E-03) is assumed to reflect the real mix of billing defects causing disputes, not a billing-db reporting artifact.

A-TARIFFLOGCOMPLETE.statement: Zero records in tariff_change_log (E-02) is assumed to mean every tariff/pricing logic change in the period would have been logged there, i.e. the log is complete.

A-AMIREJECTIONINDIRECT.statement: H-AMI-DATA-GAP was deprioritized based on E-03's read-type split alone, even though direct AMI/MDMS read-event data has not been obtained (mdms-export DEGRADED/ACCESS_PENDING), assuming billing-db's read_type field reliably reflects whether a valid AMI read was accepted.
